stories.author: Minseon Kim

stories.title: To keep drug prices high, pharma has been piling up the patents
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Pharmaceutical companies are leveraging add-on patents to extend drug patent periods.

The underlying implication is that this strategy helps maintain high drug prices.

stories.title: FurE: Efficient Instance-Specific 3D Fur Reconstruction without Animal-Fur Datasets
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces FurE, a new method for reconstructing realistic, editable 3D animal fur from multi-view images.
Addresses key challenges in fur reconstruction, including fine-scale detail, self-occlusion, and the lack of dedicated animal-fur datasets.
Employs an efficient, strand-based approach by optimizing a root-conditioned latent field to generate per-strand geometry.

stories.title: Telescopic Language Models
stories.author: Cengiz Oztireli
bullet_points: Introduces a 'Telescopic Language Model' (TLM) designed to serve multiple compute budgets efficiently.
TLM utilizes a nested-capacity Transformer architecture.
Training involves stochastic prefix supervision, balancing training on truncated prefixes against full-capacity passes.

stories.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ziwei Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of enabling unified multimodal models to self-correct their outputs (e.g., image generation).
It proposes learning 'native reflection' by jointly training the reflection text and the image generation process across the entire revision loop.
The study suggests that standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is insufficient for discovering optimal, high-success repair strategies, necessitating advanced Reinforcement Learning (RL).

stories.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
stories.author: Shimin Di
bullet_points: TokenCast addresses the high variability in token consumption when LLM agents execute tasks.
The core problem is that context window growth and dynamic decision-making make pre-execution token prediction difficult.
The proposed solution, TokenCast, learns a composable model to forecast token usage as the agent runs.

stories.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Foil' to bridge the design philosophies of Looped Transformers and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
Looped Transformers enhance model capacity by reusing fixed-size blocks, while MoE models selectively activate experts.
Foil addresses the technical challenge of effectively looping a MoE architecture to improve expert utilization.

stories.title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: Addresses the memory bottleneck in agentic LLMs caused by long context traces.
Proposes 'KV-streams' as a new, plug-and-play method for efficient context compaction.
Aims to improve training throughput by enabling efficient, trainable compaction strategies.

stories.title: Copy the Same, Distill the Difference: Initializing Linear Vision Transformers
stories.author: Hongyuan Zhu
bullet_points: The research focuses on Linear Vision Transformers (ViTs) as an alternative to standard Softmax ViTs for improved computational efficiency.
A key challenge identified is that linear ViTs typically underperform Softmax ViTs and require specialized initialization techniques.
The paper investigates whether linear ViTs can leverage knowledge or initialization strategies derived from mainstream Softmax foundation models.

stories.title: FinAutoRubric: Expert-Guided Automatic Rubric Generation for Evaluating Financial Research Agents
stories.author: Yongjae Lee
bullet_points: Introduces FinAutoRubric, a system for automatically generating evaluation rubrics for financial research AI agents.
Addresses the limitation of fixed, expert-reviewed benchmarks by allowing experts to provide reusable guidance.
Enables query-specific rubric generation and validation, accommodating diverse institutional standards.

stories.title: Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL
stories.author: Minseon Kim
bullet_points: Introduces Retrospection-Only Fine-Tuning (ROFT), a method for training AI agents.
Investigates if agents can improve future performance solely by training on explanations of past experiences, bypassing Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Suggests that self-reflection and recounting experiences are key components of human-like learning for language models.

stories.title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models
stories.author: Yulang Fei
bullet_points: Introduces Failure-Transparent Agents (FTA), a new benchmark for evaluating tool-using language models.
Addresses a critical gap where agents can falsely report success even after a required tool or process fails.
FTA isolates post-failure reporting by fixing the failed observation state, allowing for direct auditability of claims.

stories.title: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models
stories.author: Gordon Guocheng Qian
bullet_points: Introduces PDMD (Projected Distribution Matching Distillation) to address instability in video diffusion models.
Addresses the issue where standard Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) suffers from progressive oversaturation and artifacts during training.
The research mitigates critic errors that accumulate across successive student updates in complex video generation tasks.

stories.title: Unifying Distributional Training for One-Step Visual Generation
stories.author: Miao Liu
bullet_points: Introduces a unified theoretical framework for distributional training in one-step visual generation.
The framework separates distribution modeling from matching discrepancy, linking global objectives to feature updates via Wasserstein gradient flow.
Demonstrates that established methods like FD-Loss and Gaussian-kernel Drifting are recoverable within this new theoretical structure.

stories.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
stories.author: Shimin Di
bullet_points: TokenCast addresses the high variability in token consumption during LLM agent execution.
The problem stems from dynamic decision-making and the continuous inflation of context size during task runs.
The proposed method learns a composable model to forecast token usage as the agent executes.

stories.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Foil' to address the challenge of looping Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It bridges the design philosophies of Looped Transformers (reusing layers) and MoE (sparse activation).
The goal is to improve expert utilization within MoE models by enabling layer reuse.

stories.title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: Addresses the GPU memory bottleneck in scaling agentic LLMs due to long context traces.
Proposes 'KV-streams,' a new, plug-and-play strategy for efficient context compaction.
Aims to improve training throughput by enabling efficient, trainable compaction, unlike previous methods.

stories.title: Copy the Same, Distill the Difference: Initializing Linear Vision Transformers
stories.author: Hongyuan Zhu
bullet_points: Linear Vision Transformers (ViTs) aim to improve efficiency over standard Softmax ViTs by replacing attention with a linear-complexity operator.
A key challenge is that linear ViTs typically require extensive from-scratch pre-training and often underperform their Softmax counterparts.
The research addresses how to effectively initialize linear ViTs, specifically investigating if they can leverage knowledge from existing Softmax-based foundation models.

stories.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
stories.author: Andrea Zanette
bullet_points: Introduces 'harness learning,' a method to adapt the executable program (harness) that organizes language model calls and tool use.
The harness acts as the operational structure for a language-model agent, which needs adaptation based on the specific task feedback.
The approach frames the problem as meta-learning over executable programs, allowing the system to dynamically adjust its operational flow.

stories.title: Telescopic Language Models
stories.author: Cengiz Oztireli
bullet_points: Introduces the Telescopic Language Model (TLM) to address the inefficiency of training separate models for various compute budgets.
TLM is designed as a 'continuum' model, utilizing nested-capacity Transformers.
Training involves stochastic prefix supervision, where truncated prefixes are trained against the full next-token target alongside a full-capacity pass.

stories.title: Scaling Long-Form Story Generation via Narrative State Tracking
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of maintaining narrative consistency when scaling LLMs for long-form content like novels.
Introduces 'Narrative State Tracking Agent' (NstAgent), a training-free agentic framework.
Aims to extend current story generation capabilities beyond the typical 10,000-word limit.

stories.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Foil' to bridge the design philosophies of Looped Transformers and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
Looped Transformers reuse fixed-size models multiple times to increase parameter utilization, while MoE models selectively activate experts.
Foil addresses the technical challenge of effectively looping a MoE architecture to enhance expert usage.

stories.title: Towards Communication-Efficient Social Intelligence in Language Agents
stories.author: Hui Xiong
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of making language agents socially intelligent by requiring them to negotiate and coordinate.
Proposes Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT) to improve social goal attainment.
Focuses on reducing communication cost by ensuring agents convey only necessary information to respect participant constraints.

stories.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
stories.author: Andrea Zanette
bullet_points: Introduces 'harness learning' to adapt language model agents for diverse tasks.
The 'harness' is the executable program controlling model calls, tool use, and information flow.
The method uses meta-learning over executable programs, guided by task execution feedback, to revise the harness.

stories.title: Reinforcing Agentic Creativity in Scientific Ideation with Night Science
stories.author: Sujay Kumar Jauhar
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of LLMs' low-entropy bias in generating creative, open-ended scientific ideas.
Introduces 'AI Night-Scientist,' an agentic framework leveraging reinforcement learning.
Aims to bridge the gap between structured 'day science' and serendipitous 'night science' in AI ideation.

stories.title: Rethinking Personalized Generation: Test-Time Alignment via Factorized Ranking Models
stories.author: Zhe Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of standard LLM alignment paradigms which optimize for monolithic user preferences.
It proposes using test-time alignment to unlock significant, untapped performance headroom for personalized generation.
The work suggests that personalized generation is well-suited for test-time scaling methods, such as Best-of-N (BoN).

stories.title: AI Agent Governance on AWS: Block Agents, Prove EU AI Act Compliance
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Demonstrates practical application of AI Agent Governance using AWS Bedrock.

stories.title: Count It or Compute It: When a Tool Returns Rows, the Models That Count Them Right Spend the Tokens
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article highlights a critical, often overlooked aspect of LLM agent performance: accurately counting the results returned by tools.
Models that attempt to reason through a list of returned rows consume significantly more tokens (6x to 26x) compared to models given a direct count.
The benchmark suggests a trade-off between computational cost (tokens) and accuracy when agents interact with tool outputs.
